name: # Officestock — Office
brief:
# Officestock — Office Supplies Inventory Tracker

## What this is
An internal tool to track office supplies (stationery, printer consumables,
kitchen and cleaning items) so nothing runs out unannounced. Staff record what
they take; the office manager receives deliveries and runs stocktakes.

## Users
- **Staff** — take an item from the cupboard.
- **Office manager** — receive deliveries, adjust counts, run stocktakes.
- **Approver** — approve purchase requests raised below reorder level.

## Core domain
- **Item**: id, name, category (Stationery | Printer | Kitchen | Cleaning |
  Tech), unit (each / box / ream / pack), current qty, reorder level, target
  qty (to top up to), location, active.
- **Movement**: id, item, delta (+/-), reason (Issued | Received | Damaged |
  Adjustment | Stocktake), actor, timestamp, note, resulting qty.
- **PurchaseRequest**: id, item, requested qty, status (Open | Approved |
  Ordered | Received | Cancelled), raised-by, decision note.

## Required features
1. **Item list** — searchable, filterable by category and by a "needs reorder"
   toggle; each row shows qty, reorder level, a colour-coded status, and
   location. Sort by name, qty, or category.
2. **Issue an item** — pick item, quantity, actor; refuse if quantity exceeds
   current stock; write an Issued movement and decrement qty.
3. **Receive stock** — increase qty and write a Received movement; if an Open/
   Approved/Ordered purchase request exists for that item, mark it Received.
4. **Adjust / damage** — record a Damaged or Adjustment movement; an adjustment
   requires a note and can set the qty to a counted value (the delta is
   computed), never silently.
5. **Purchase requests** — raise a request for a below-reorder item with a
   suggested quantity of (target − current); approve, order, receive, cancel
   with constrained transitions; receiving a request writes a Received movement.
6. **Stocktake** — enter a counted qty per item in a category; for each item the
   app writes a Stocktake movement whose delta is counted − current, and shows a
   variance report (items over/under by more than a threshold).
7. **Dashboard** — total items, count below reorder, open purchase requests, and
   total value on hand if an optional unit cost is set per item.

## Functional requirements
- Quantities are non-negative integers; stock can never go negative (issuing
  more than on hand is refused naming the shortfall).
- Current qty is the running sum of movements; a reconstruction from the
  movement log must equal the stored qty (invariant check exposed).
- Purchase-request status transitions constrained: Open→Approved→Ordered→
  Received (or →Cancelled from Open/Approved/Ordered); Received is terminal.
- Suggested reorder qty = max(0, target − current).
- Optional value on hand = qty × unit cost (integer pence), displayed GBP.

## Non-functional requirements
- Desktop-first, usable to 768px; accessible tables and forms.
- Deterministic inventory logic separated from UI for unit testing.
- Local persistence; no external services required.

## Explicitly out of scope
- Barcode scanning.
- Supplier ordering / EDI integration.
- Asset depreciation or accounting.
- Multi-site inventory.

# Movement Requests

Replenishment Movement Requests Replenishment movement requests are requests that are generated by min-max planning to replenish material when a minimum quantity for a specific item is reached. Replenishment movement requests replenish material that's sourced from a different location within the same inventory organization.

Source: https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/supply-chain-and-manufacturing/25d/famml/movement-requests.html

artifacts.title: Phase narrative (LLM)
artifacts.body:
Phase 0 deep research confirms that office-supply tracking is a well-defined, low-complexity problem space with strong demand for a lightweight internal tool: manual office stock management consistently produces stockouts, over-ordering, and wasted budget, while existing solutions fall into two camps—spreadsheet templates (movement-driven Excel/Sheets trackers with auto-reorder alerts, dashboards, and pre-loaded SKU catalogs) and full stock-management software that is heavier than a small office needs. Core mechanics are well-established across sources: goods flow from receiving inspection through material requests, inventory issues, returns, and delivery confirmation, with replenishment triggered by min-max planning when an item hits its minimum quantity. For Officestock, this validates a narrow MVP centered on movement-driven stock (staff record takes; office manager receives deliveries, adjusts counts, and runs stocktakes), low-stock/reorder alerts against min-max thresholds, and a simple dashboard—deliberately spreadsheet-simple in UX, not a warehouse system—with the feasibility takeaway that the critical design work is modeling the movement ledger and reorder rules, not novel technology.

# Phase Narrative — Office (P7: Domain & Market Research)

Domain and market research confirms that office supply management is a well-defined, method-driven problem space with an established vocabulary (reorder points, par levels, safety stock, consumption tracking) and strong demand for a lightweight internal solution. The competitive landscape splits into two camps: sophisticated Excel/Google Sheets templates with auto-reorder alerts and live dashboards (a 2026 movement-driven tracker ships with a pre-loaded 25-SKU catalog), and online tools like Stackby that bundle asset tracking with automated reorders for free. What none of these offer is a purpose-built, role-aware workflow matching Officestock's exact model—staff logging consumptions, office managers receiving deliveries and running stocktakes—so the market research validates the design premise while confirming the free-template baseline against which Officestock's simplicity, accessibility, and no-setup experience must differentiate.

artifacts.title: Phase narrative (LLM)
artifacts.body:
As Officestock moves into P11, the initiative pivots from a static tracker toward a real-time, augmented inventory platform, driven by the recurring pain points surfaced across office stock management research: manual tracking causes stockouts, over-ordering, and wasted budget, and teams need live visibility rather than periodic counts. The phase centers on connecting the existing take/receive/stocktake workflows to min-max planning logic—where replenishment movement requests are automatically generated when an item hits its minimum quantity—and surfacing that data through a consolidated Power BI-style dashboard showing stock levels, reorder status, and movement history in one interface. Tool augmentation also means wiring Officestock's data into the broader Microsoft ecosystem, mirroring how Dynamics 365 inventory data can feed Power BI reports for stock movement, aging, and reorder frequency, so the office manager gets automated reorder alerts instead of discovering an empty cupboard. The throughline for this phase is turning reactive record-keeping into proactive, real-time replenishment intelligence built for office teams.

## Mission
# Officestock — Office Supplies Inventory Tracker

## What this is
An internal tool to track office supplies (stationery, printer consumables,
kitchen and cleaning items) so nothing runs out unannounced. Staff record what
they take; the office manager receives deliveries and runs stocktakes.

## Users
- **Staff** — take an item from the cupboard.
- **Office manager** — receive deliveries, adjust counts, run stocktakes.
- **Approver** — approve purchase requests raised below reorder level.

## Core domain
- **Item**: id, name, category (Stationery | Printer | Kitchen | Cleaning |
  Tech), unit (each / box / ream / pack), current qty, reorder level, target
  qty (to top up to), location, active.
- **Movement**: id, item, delta (+/-), reason (Issued | Received | Damaged |
  Adjustment | Stocktake), actor, timestamp, note, resulting qty.
- **PurchaseRequest**: id, item, requested qty, status (Open | Approved |
  Ordered | Received | Cancelled), raised-by, decision note.

## Required features
1. **Item list** — searchable, filterable by category and by a "needs reorder"
   toggle; each row shows qty, reorder level, a colour-coded status, and
   location. Sort by name, qty, or category.
2. **Issue an item** — pick item, quantity, actor; refuse if quantity exceeds
   current stock; write an Issued movement and decrement qty.
3. **Receive stock** — increase qty and write a Received movement; if an Open/
   Approved/Ordered purchase request exists for that item, mark it Received.
4. **Adjust / damage** — record a Damaged or Adjustment movement; an adjustment
   requires a note and can set the qty to a counted value (the delta is
   computed), never silently.
5. **Purchase requests** — raise a request for a below-reorder item with a
   suggested quantity of (target − current); approve, order, receive, cancel
   with constrained transitions; receiving a request writes a Received movement.
6. **Stocktake** — enter a counted qty per item in a category; for each item the
   app writes a Stocktake movement whose delta is counted − current, and shows a
   variance report (items over/under by more than a threshold).
7. **Dashboard** — total items, count below reorder, open purchase requests, and
   total value on hand if an optional unit cost is set per item.

## Functional requirements
- Quantities are non-negative integers; stock can never go negative (issuing
  more than on hand is refused naming the shortfall).
- Current qty is the running sum of movements; a reconstruction from the
  movement log must equal the stored qty (invariant check exposed).
- Purchase-request status transitions constrained: Open→Approved→Ordered→
  Received (or →Cancelled from Open/Approved/Ordered); Received is terminal.
- Suggested reorder qty = max(0, target − current).

- Desktop-first, usable to 768px; accessible tables and forms.
- Deterministic inventory logic separated from UI for unit testing.
- Local persistence; no external services required.

- Supplier ordering / EDI integration.
- Asset depreciation or accounting.
- Multi-site inventory.
